# Mara Voss

<!-- bm:block id=opening preset=lead label="Opening statement" -->
I photograph places that take time to reach. The work is less about the landmark than about the hours
around it — the light that arrives late, the weather that refuses to clear, the small window when stone
and sky agree.

This page collects three field seasons across the Alps, the Faroe Islands, and the Icelandic highlands.
Everything below is drawn from the same negative archive, processed without composite skies.
<!-- bm:/block -->

Most of these frames were made on foot, carrying a medium-format body and a tripod that I complain
about daily. The result is a body of work that favors patience over spectacle. Prints are made in
small editions from a single darkroom in Innsbruck.

<!-- bm:block preset=hero focal={"x":0.5,"y":0.35} -->
![Dolomite ridgeline at first light](images/dolomites.svg)

**The starting point:** a ridge at dawn, made after a four-hour approach in the dark.
<!-- bm:/block -->

## A working method

- Return to a location until the weather turns.
- Expose for the shadow, never for the sky.
- Keep the horizon honest — no crop that invents a view.

> A landscape photograph is a record of waiting, not a record of standing somewhere.

---

# Dolomites, three winters

The Dolomites series is the oldest in the archive and the one I understand least. Each winter the same
ridges look unfamiliar, and the photographs follow that confusion rather than resolving it. The work is
about repetition — the same walk, made again, until something finally changes.

<!-- bm:columns id=dolomites-split weights=[2,1] label="Series and print facts" -->
<!-- bm:col label="The series" -->
## Snow that stays

The series opens at the end of the storm, when the valleys are quiet and the ridgelines hold their
first clean light. I work slowly here, often making a single frame in a morning.

1. Approach before first light.
2. Wait for the cloud to lift off the ridge.
3. Expose once, and leave before the light flattens.

![Ridge snow and low cloud](images/dolomites-ridge.svg)

# A wider selection

The gallery draws from all three field seasons rather than a single trip. It is arranged by light

# Faroe Islands

The Faroes are the noisiest place I have photographed — wind, water, and birds in constant motion. The
series tries to hold that restlessness still for a moment without pretending it has stopped.

<!-- bm:columns id=faroe-cards label="Field notes" -->
<!-- bm:col preset=card -->
## 1. Arrive

![Cliff edge in grey weather](images/faroe.svg)

The first days are for walking, not photographing. The scale only becomes legible after the weather
has had time to change around you.

<!-- bm:col preset=card -->
## 2. Wait

![Cloud moving across the headland](images/faroe-cloud.svg)

Most mornings offer nothing. The few that offer something tend to do so within twenty minutes, and
then close again for the rest of the day.

<!-- bm:col preset=card -->
## 3. Print

![Grass roof and stone wall](images/faroe-village.svg)

The prints are deliberately quiet. These are places that resist drama, and the paper should not argue
with them.
<!-- bm:/columns -->

> Weather is not an obstacle to the photograph. It is the subject.

# Notes on process

## A note about the negatives

<!-- bm:block id=negative-note preset=note label="Darkroom note" -->
### Note: every negative is the source

No frame in this portfolio is a composite, and no sky has been replaced. If a print needed a different
photograph behind it, the frame was not included.

<!-- bm:/block -->

<!-- bm:block id=rights-warning preset=warning label="Usage warning" -->
### Warning: prints are licensed, not transferred

Purchasing a print does not transfer reproduction rights. Editorial requests should go through the
studio, and commercial use is handled case by case.

<!-- bm:/block -->

## Two separately movable statements

<!-- bm:block id=equipment label="The equipment" -->
**Equipment:** a single medium-format body, one lens, and a tripod that has been repaired twice.
<!-- bm:/block -->

<!-- bm:block id=equipment-rationale label="Why so little" -->
**Rationale:** a limited kit forces a decision before the light arrives, not during it.

A second block. Editing either statement must never merge it with the other.
<!-- bm:/block -->

# Prints and commissions

Work is available as editioned silver and pigment prints, and as commissioned series for editorial and
institutional clients. Commissions usually involve a minimum of two visits to a location so that the
first trip can be spent learning rather than photographing.
